contract.text: An unposted pick whose committed game is postponed, cancelled or missing from the schedule is regenerated from live games; a locked slot whose game is postponed/cancelled is void (neither hit nor miss) and does not block result polling.

mechanism.text: run_single_check short-circuited as 'Pick already locked' whenever the existing pick's primary game had abstract status other than 'P'; a postponed game is not 'P', so the stale unposted pick was kept and the cascade never ran to replace it
grading had no void result: a locked slot whose game was postponed/cancelled could not be scored as a Pass, so a double-down day could not be scored from the played slot

candidate filtering and lock-gap decisions used abstract statuses only, so candidates from games that were abstract-Preview but detailed-Postponed stayed eligible

contract.text: The deployed service behaves as its code, config and docs state: the scheduler works the ET contest day and feeds the systemd watchdog through every wait; each EOD health check evaluates the processed date, alerts on its documented condition and never goes silent on a crash; a missed delivery is alerted before first pitch (missed_pick_alert_min); pick/streak writes cannot tear and a pick is delivered at most once; live decision inputs match what training/backtest used, shadow features are leak-free, and neither the dashboard nor the deploy path exposes picks or the root key.

mechanism.text: run_day's EOD run_all_checks call passed no today=, so the day-keyed Tier-1 checks (post_failure, postponed_pick, fallback_defer, analytics_artifacts_missing) evaluated date.today(): an EOD run after midnight checked D+1, found no pick and returned no alert for D

bts schedule without --date took datetime.now(timezone.utc) and the scheduler unit passes no --date, so a scheduler restart between ~20:00 and 24:00 ET (deploy, OOM, watchdog) began run_day for the next date and abandoned that night's result polling, late-slate delivery, DH game 2 and EOD health

the doubleheader game-2 recheck looped a bare time.sleep(dh_recheck_min*60) (15 min default, up to 10x) without watchdog pings, so two sleeps exceeded WatchdogSec=1800 and systemd SIGABRTed the daemon into a crash-restart loop on an unlocked-pick DH day
on a no-games day run_day returned at the 'No games scheduled' guard with no idle sleep, so Restart=always relaunched it every ~30 s all day, spiking NRestarts into a false restart_spike

health contest_state.check measured the lag as calendar days, gap_days = (latest resolved pick - source_date).days (the 58c9adc form), so a multi-day no-pick stretch (off-days, All-Star break) would inflate the gap into a false 'STALE' CRITICAL on the first day back
the health runner's _safe_run caught any check exception, logged it and returned [], so a check that raised every run produced no alert and no DM
predicted_vs_realized.evaluate counted n14 over the whole lookback and never enforced min_days_28d, so early-season drift could go CRITICAL on near-identical overlapping 14d/28d windows

reconcile_results recomputed the streak with a backward walk that stopped at the first miss without replaying the 10-15 saver, so the nightly reconcile under-counted a saver-preserved streak in streak.json
the blend averaged each model's game probability per batter_id, so a batter in both games of a doubleheader got one probability mixing both matchups, mapped back to both rows
_fetch_prior_lineup hardcoded startDate=2026-03-20&endDate=2026-12-31, so from 2027 the projected-lineup fallback would return 2026 lineups (no effect inside the 2026 season)

compute_all_features rolled the shadow CONTEXT column batter_hard_contact_30g over PA rows (window 120) with one shift(1) across the batter-sorted series, so each batter's first row inherited the previous batter's value and the window kept same-date PAs: leakage in the context-stack shadow model and its promotion eval

contract.text: The decision streak and the dashboard's real-streak figure equal the real MLB contest streak (last confirmed) and are never raised by the model's replay of suggested picks; a current contest activeStreak is persisted even when per-round coverage lags.

derive_source_date's RESOLVED set omitted MLB's profile value 'not_hit', so settled misses did not count toward source_date, biasing freshness against reset days

the noon-ET escalation (4f13eb3) read a one-step source_date gap persisting past noon as a possible missed entry, but that gap is the normal coverage lag of the per-round array, so it produced a daily false WARN; gap >= 2 could page a false CRITICAL on a transient ledger lag

the fallback re-evaluated at its deadline, got pick_result None (a genuine MDP skip) and, treating it as 'no fresh pick, use cached', delivered and locked the stale provisional pick

three checks read an undelivered pick file as a failure on a deliberate-skip day — the E3 missed-pick alert, the EOD post_failure CRITICAL and analytics_artifacts_missing (pick_locked-or-delivered heuristic) — so a correctly undelivered file raises false alerts

records.tier_reason: no harmful firing is evidenced for any link; tier A by the B -> A rule: unfixed residuals (streak/pick two-file pair under a crash, postponed cached-fallback delivery, manual-run and final-fallback lineup-gate bypasses, F6 fingerprint scope, best-effort churn check) can still change state, delivery or alerting; F3 (liveness), F8/F12 (recoverability), F13 (state) and F2/R4 (delivery) are A-class if they fire

contract.text: Each audited path meets its contract: a normal early lock commits only lineup-confirmed selected slots whose games are still available (F2, R4); a torn state file never yields a crash loop that monitors score healthy (F3); a crashing health check surfaces CRITICAL (F4); realized_calibration evaluates the current regime's last 30 days once 5 bucket picks exist (F6); an interrupted R2 sync leaves the prior manifest restorable (F8); the skip-shadow verdict and its breakeven are reproducible from the repo and valid under nightly re-looks (F10); the repo's tracked units reproduce production (F12); each result changes streak state at most once (F13); and `bts preview` defaults to tomorrow in ET (F15).
contract.source: F2: strategy.should_lock docstring condition 2 at 9643d83; R4: design §10.3 postponed cached-fallback oracle ('no delivery naming a postponed game') + 6d74d39 R4; F3: util.atomic_write_text docstring (audit D1) at a349ac5; F4: health/runner.py _safe_run docstring (audit H3, 0f2bc3c); F6: health/realized_calibration.py module docstring (30-day lookback, minimum bucket count 5); F8: data/sync.py sync_to_r2 docstring 'Writes the manifest last, atomically' at cca6761; F10: docs/audit/2026-06-20-skip-policy-shadow.md (verdict vs the 0.744 breakeven) + audit F10; F12: audit memo raw finding 12 (DR from the tracked unit); F13: design §10.3 scoring crash/restart oracle ('one result affects streak and saver at most once') + ARCHITECTURE.md 'Scoring serialization'; F15: cli.py preview --date help 'Defaults to tomorrow' + the _today_et ET convention

mechanism.text: F2: should_lock rejected only a projected primary and _lock_decision_from_predictions passed only daily.pick, so on a double day a projected double-down rode the primary's confirmation through the normal early lock (the gap rule was built for a single pick racing projected alternatives)

F3: save_state wrote scheduler_state.json with a bare write_text and load_state parsed it with no recovery, while run_day wrote the RUNNING heartbeat and signalled READY/watchdog before loading state; a torn file would crash every start and restart every 30 s with a fresh heartbeat, check_heartbeat scored any fresh 'running' heartbeat healthy, restart_spike ran only at EOD inside the crashing process and the deploy canary checked is-active at +30 s

F4: calibration, projected_lineup, post_failure and disk_fill caught exceptions inside check() and returned [], so an evaluation failure looked healthy and never reached _safe_run's CRITICAL-on-crash conversion (the audit-H3 contract)

F6: realized_calibration.check dropped every pick whose run_time preceded the latest deploy stamp and every deploy (docs, shadow, ops) re-stamped, so the bucket sample could not reach min_bucket_n while deploys were frequent and the check was effectively dead

F8: sync_to_r2 overwrote stable object keys before replacing the manifest, so an interrupted sync left the old manifest pointing at new bytes; sync_from_r2 downloaded into the final path and deleted it on a checksum mismatch; verify_manifest checked only manifest metadata and age

F10: the skip-policy shadow re-tested a fixed-N 95% Wilson interval against the 0.744 breakeven at every nightly rebuild (repeated looks, not time-uniform), and the breakeven's derivation existed only as /tmp/skip_qdelta.py on the box, outside the repo

F12: the tracked scripts/bts-scheduler.service was the stale Pi5 unit (Type=simple, /home/stonehengee paths, Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=300) while production ran notify + watchdog with Restart=always/30 s; no dashboard unit was tracked and nothing detected drift, so a rebuild from the repo would install a broken unit

F13: check-results (01:00 cron) and the daemon's result polling (until 05:00) each did load pick -> resolve -> update_streak -> save_pick with no shared lock (only saver state had a flock), and the daemon's cap/unresolved/suspended writers and the 02:00 reconcile_results also wrote unlocked, so an interleave could double-apply or lose a streak update or overwrite a terminal result
F15: bts preview computed its default date as UTC now + 1 day, so a manual run between about 20:00 and 23:59 ET wrote the slate for the day after tomorrow (the 03:00 ET cron was unaffected)

R4: _lock_decision_from_predictions status-filtered contender rows but not the already-selected pick/double-down, so a selected game that went postponed or started between selection and lock could ride its stale lineup flag into delivery
